findings.failure_scenario: A user upgrading crewAI whose code contains `from crewai.tasks.task_guardrail import TaskGuardrail` or `from crewai.utilities.events import TaskGuardrailStartedEvent` (import paths that existed in the baseline release and are shown in the shipped docs) gets ModuleNotFoundError/ImportError at import time; a repo-wide search confirms no task_guardrail.py shim, no alias, and no DeprecationWarning path was added anywhere in the tree.
findings.summary: The rename deletes the previously shipped public module crewai.tasks.task_guardrail (TaskGuardrail, TaskGuardrailResult) and crewai.utilities.events.task_guardrail_events (TaskGuardrailStartedEvent, TaskGuardrailCompletedEvent) with no deprecated alias or re-export, so existing user imports of those names fail after upgrade.

findings.failure_scenario: An external observability or alerting pipeline (the event bus is explicitly documented for external event handling and BaseEvent.to_json() serializes the `type` field) that filters on event.type == "task_guardrail_started" receives no matching events after the upgrade, so guardrail monitoring silently stops reporting with no error raised; persisted event logs from before and after the upgrade also no longer group under one discriminator.
findings.summary: The event wire discriminator changed from type "task_guardrail_started"/"task_guardrail_completed" to "llm_guardrail_started"/"llm_guardrail_completed" with no compatibility mapping, silently breaking external consumers that filter serialized events on the type field.
